pedagogy.learning_objective: Distinguish the equal-weight mean of six per-sequence proportions from the proportion pooled over eight eligible transitions.
assumptions: Independent fair coin flips with fixed probability 1/2
Exactly three flips in each equally likely sequence
Exclude sequences with no observed flip after heads when averaging defined per-sequence rates
Assign equal weight to each retained sequence, not to each eligible transition
limitations: The 5/12 result concerns this finite-sequence estimator, not the next-flip probability
The three-flip example supplies no universal basketball shooting bonus
This is a conceptual introduction; basketball inference needs data and an appropriate null model
pedagogy.challenge: Enumerate all eight three-flip sequences; mark the two with no eligible transition, compare the mean of the six defined rates with the pooled proportion.
pedagogy.expected_learning: The learner explains why 5/12 and 1/2 answer different averaging questions and why the next independent fair-coin flip remains 50 percent.

sources.title: Miller & Sanjurjo (2018), Surprised by the Hot Hand Fallacy? A Truth in the Law of Small Numbers, Econometrica 86(6), 2019–2047
sources.locator: Abstract and Section 1, Table 1 (three-flip sequences); discussion of equal sequence weights versus recorded flips.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Introduce the basketball motivation and the possibility of biased estimation.

claims.statement: The historical hot-hand debate and estimation bias are documented in Miller and Sanjurjo; no particular player improvement is claimed.
claims.script_quote: Учёные спорили об этом десятилетиями. Оказалось, даже способ подсчёта может спрятать эффект!
claims.reasoning: The historical hot-hand debate and estimation bias are documented in Miller and Sanjurjo; no particular player improvement is claimed.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Separate the probability of a future independent flip from a statistic computed from finite sequences.

claims.statement: An independent fair coin has next-head probability 1/2 regardless of previous flips.
claims.script_quote: У честной монетки без памяти шанс следующего орла всегда пятьдесят процентов.
claims.reasoning: An independent fair coin has next-head probability 1/2 regardless of previous flips.
claims.proof: Independence is the explicit model assumption (coin without memory): P(H_next and H_previous)=P(H_next)P(H_previous)=1/4. Thus P(H_next|H_previous)=(1/4)/(1/2)=1/2. Fairness alone without independence would not establish this.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Display the six defined rates and give the exact mean, with excluded sequences explained in narration.

claims.statement: Two of eight sequences have no observable flip following heads; averaging the six remaining rates equally gives 5/12, not a changed next-flip probability.
claims.script_quote: Подходящих серий шесть. В двух остальных после орла нет броска: их пропускаем. Усредняем шесть долей с одинаковым весом — получаем примерно сорок два процента!
claims.reasoning: Two of eight sequences have no observable flip following heads; averaging the six remaining rates equally gives 5/12, not a changed next-flip probability.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Contrast the pooled 4/8 rate with the equal-sequence mean and state the boundary of the basketball analogy.

claims.statement: The same eligible transitions contain four heads out of eight; changing weights changes the estimand.
claims.script_quote: Если объединить все подходящие переходы, получим четыре орла из восьми — пятьдесят процентов.
claims.reasoning: The same eligible transitions contain four heads out of eight; changing weights changes the estimand.

claims.statement: Streak-selection bias is relevant to basketball analyses, but its size depends on the design, so the coin example supplies no universal bonus.
claims.script_quote: В баскетболе такое смещение тоже нужно учитывать. Но этот пример не вычисляет бонус точности игрока.
claims.reasoning: Streak-selection bias is relevant to basketball analyses, but its size depends on the design, so the coin example supplies no universal bonus.

scene_reviews.teaching_role: Ask the learner to enumerate outcomes and explain which weights each mean uses.

claims.statement: Three binary flips have eight possible sequences.
claims.script_quote: выпиши все восемь серий по три броска.
claims.reasoning: Three binary flips have eight possible sequences.
claims.proof: Each of three positions has two outcomes, yielding 2×2×2=8; two have no eligible transition.

claims.statement: Two consecutive makes by themselves do not establish a hot-hand effect; the task concerns comparing two estimators.
claims.script_quote: А по двум попаданиям подряд не спеши объявлять себя непобедимым!
claims.reasoning: Two consecutive makes by themselves do not establish a hot-hand effect; the task concerns comparing two estimators.

scientific.scope: Current lesson source, evidence, mathematics and teaching design only; no new playback, timing or pronunciation approval.

evidence_matches_claims.rationale: The paper introduction supports historical estimation bias in basketball; Table 1 supports the three-flip example. The dossier gives a conditional-independence proof for the 50 percent next-head probability.

calculations_correct.rationale: Independently enumerated all eight sequences. Six have defined rates with equal-weight mean 5/12; eight eligible transitions contain four heads, yielding a pooled 1/2.

assumptions_and_limits.rationale: Narration specifies a fair coin without memory, fixes sequence length at three, and explains exclusion of two rows; the challenge preserves that exclusion.

no_overclaim.rationale: Revised narration and caption limit the number to the coin example and explain relevance to counting basketball streaks without assigning a shooting bonus.

pedagogical.scope: Current lesson source, evidence, mathematics and teaching design only; no new playback, timing or pronunciation approval.

age_and_prerequisites.rationale: A 12-year-old with fractions, percentages and means can work through three flips on paper; the basketball hook supplies a concrete purpose.

objective_alignment.rationale: The same outcomes are summarized first with equal sequence weights and then per eligible transition, directly addressing the objective.

explanation_clarity.rationale: The worked OOR row identifies O,R as its two follow-ups, giving 1/2. The next scene groups all eight follow-ups and shows that row contributing two observations.

challenge_checks_understanding.rationale: The learner reconstructs eight sequences, identifies the two without eligible follow-ups, and compares the summaries. Missing a follow-up or treating an undefined row as zero yields a checkable error.
